    All Classes and Interfaces

    Class
    Description
    AgentController
    Turns the network's choice into the same inputs a person produces: the camera is turned through the mouse-look path and keys are held through their key bindings.
    AgentSession
    Something SwordAI is doing in the world from a command until it is stopped: training, a fight with the network playing the user's character, or sparring against it.
    Arena
    A walled stone platform high above the world.
    ArenaDriver
    Something that plays the agent's body from the server thread instead of from a game client: training without the screen, where the agent is a fake player too.
    ArenaServer
    Everything that happens on the integrated server while the agent trains: the arena, the sparring bot, episode resets and the bookkeeping of who hit whom.
    ArenaServer.HitCount
    Swings that reached the other fighter, by what they came to.
    AvatarRendererMixin
    Lets KeyedSkin repaint other players after vanilla has decided how to draw them.
    BlindGuard
    Watches for a picture that has no opponent in it although the opponent is right in front of the camera.
    BotBrain
    The scripted mind of the sparring bot.
    BotPilot
    Lets the trained network play a fake player, so that a person (or the network itself) can fight it.
    CombatLog
    Collects combat events on the server thread until the client thread's next decision picks them up.
    Commands
    The /swordai command.
    DebugDump
    Saves exactly what the agent was shown: the raw frame, the masks extracted from it and the mask statistics.
    DemoPlan
    /swordai demo [kind]: the user fights the training's scripted opponents themselves, in the training's own arena and on its own terms, while each step is recorded the way the network would have seen and done it (DemoFile), to be learned from (Config.demoWeight).
    EntityMixin
    Lets a training fight show its opponent late, as a server would: every move the game is told of comes through here, and the opponent's are kept back for a few ticks.
    EpisodePlan
    What the client asks the server to set up for the next episode.
    FakeFall
    How far a fake player has fallen, counted here because the game does not count it.
    FightLearnSession
    /swordai fight that the network also learns from: it plays the user's own character against another player, in whatever world or server the user is in, and every fight is gathered, scored with the rewards of the stage it is in, and learned from.
    FightSession
    The trained network plays the user's own character against another player, in whatever world or server the user is in.
    FightTrace
    A training fight against a scripted opponent, tick by tick, for reading afterwards how a fight was lost: the distance, both swords (the opponent's as the server has it), who is on the ground and how the opponent is moving, the keys and which rule pressed them, the tactic, and every hit either way with whether it was critical.
    FrameGrabber
    Reads the rendered frame back from the GPU through the same device calls vanilla's screenshot code uses, so it works on whatever graphics backend the game runs on.
    FramerateLimitTrackerMixin
    Vanilla drops to ten frames a second when the window is minimised or nobody has touched the keyboard for a while.
    GameRendererMixin
    Tells the frame grabber the moment the world is complete in the main render target: the hand pass starts by flushing everything the level left queued, and nothing of the hand, the screen effects, the HUD or an open screen has been drawn yet.
    HeadlessSession
    Training without the screen.
    KeyedSkin
    While the agent is running, the opponent is drawn with a flat two-colour skin (blue head, green body) and without anything that would cover or tint it.
    KeyMappingAccessor
    Which physical key a binding currently sits on.
    KeyMappingMixin
    While the agent plays, presses on the real keyboard and mouse do not reach the key bindings, so clicking back into the window or leaning on a key cannot swing, drop the sword or change the hotbar slot.
    KnockbackLag
    The opponent's own connection to the server.
    KnockbackLag.Pending
     
    LivingEntityMixin
    Lets a training fight knock its opponent back a few ticks late, as a player with a connection of its own is.
    LoadedFighter
    The saved network, loaded to play rather than to learn.
    LocalPlayerMixin
    A person's mouse moves the view every frame; the agent turns once per game tick.
    MinecraftMixin
    Vanilla reads the keys only while no screen is open, and opening one lets go of all of them.
    ModelPack
    A trained model as one file, to keep or to take to another game: /swordai export writes one to swordai/models, /swordai import puts one back.
    MouseHandlerMixin
    While the agent plays, moving the physical mouse must not turn the player.
    Observer
    Builds the two views of a moment in the game: the observation the agent acts on (pixels and its own body) and the ground truth used only to score it.
    Opponents
    What a fight in someone's world needs to know about the players around, whether or not it is learned from.
    OptionsGuard
    Puts the game options into the state the agent's vision and controls assume, and puts them back afterwards.
    OwnSwing
    The last attack the player's own character made, as their game client made it out: how charged the weapon was, and whether the game will call the hit a sprint hit, a critical hit or a sweep.
    PairedEval
    A paired evaluation in one run (Config.pairedBase): every fight of a frozen measurement is fought twice, by this run's network (A) and by another one (B), from the same seed, so that the two share everything the run brings (its connection, its timing, the machine) and differ only in how they fight.
    PlayerAttackMixin
    Records how charged the weapon was, whether the attacker was sprinting and whether it was falling at the instant an attack starts.
    ReplicaBody
    A fake player run as if it had a game client of its own.
    ReplicaBody.Seen
    Everything about the opponent that decides how it is shown, as of one tick.
    ReplicaTrainer
    Training in which the agent's body is a fake player, run as if it had a game client of its own (ReplicaBody), with a picture that is drawn for it rather than read off the screen.
    Report
    Assembles the text behind /swordai report: enough to tune the training from, short enough to paste.
    RoundRecorder
    Every round of /swordai fight, tick by tick, for working out afterwards why a round was lost and what the opponent did: the distance, both swords, the keys and which rule pressed them, how the opponent moved, and every hit either way with what kind it was likely to be.
    RoundRecorder.Tick
    One tick, as recorded.
    SeenLag
    Lag for the opponent on the screen.
    SeenLag.Move
    News of a move, exactly as the game was about to take it in.
    SelfTest
    Checks, in the real game, that the agent's eyes work before any training time is spent: the bot is stood at known spots and the masks must show it where and as large as geometry predicts, and show nothing at all when it is behind the camera.
    Sightline
    Where a fighter's crosshair is in relation to its opponent: ground truth, used only to score it.
    SparLearnSession
    Sparring that the network also learns from.
    SparPilot
    Whatever plays the fake player while a person spars against it: the trained network as it is (BotPilot), or the network while it also learns from the fight.
    SparSession
    The user fights the trained network themselves.
    StyleWatch
    Counts how the opponent of a /swordai fight fights, from what this game can see of it, into that player's PersonStyle: where it keeps its distance, whether it answers the fighter's hits on its way down, whether it comes after a fighter that backs off with a hit from the air, how far a hit sends it, whether it jumps with the hits it takes.
    SwordAi
     
    SwordAiClient
     
    SwordAiScreen
    The SwordAI menu: everything the /swordai command does that is used day to day, as buttons, and the saved models.
    SwordAiScreen.Label
    A line of text placed by SwordAiScreen.init(), drawn over the panels.
    SwordAiScreen.Page
     
    SwordAiScreen.Panel
    A box drawn behind a group of buttons, with its heading.
    SwordFiles
    Everything SwordAI keeps on disk lives in <game dir>/swordai.
    SwordFiles.LostCasesFile
     
    Trainer
    Training as such: which fight comes next, what a step was worth, when the network learns from what it has gathered, and when a stage is passed.
    Trainer.Mode
     
    Trainer.Phase
     
    Trainer.PingCount
    What the fights against one kind of connection came to.
    TrainingSession
    Training on the screen: the agent plays the user's own character and sees the frames the game draws.
    Truth
    Snapshot of the arena, published by the server thread once per tick and read by the client thread.
    WeatherEffectRendererMixin
    Leaves rain and snow out of the agent's picture.
    WindowGuard
    Makes the game window small while training runs faster than real time, and puts it back afterwards.
